## Cyrus data pack studio (R2)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r4` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN 2b, 4.3, 4.11, R2 days 13-14; research `A2-datapacks.md`. **Nothing is deployed or switched on.** Two flags, both OFF by default (fail closed): `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO=1` (portal: the build request may get the data pack route) and `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL=1` (worker: a built data pack may be placed on a server). Off, every build request is byte-identical to before and no code touches a server. Data packs are **not plan-gated** (owner decision for composition features): no plan lookup happens for them. Host seam: no new Nxeon imports (the delivery uses the existing `MemberPlacer` from `lib/cyrus/modpack/install.ts`), no new tables, no foreign keys; assets go into the existing `CyrusProjectAsset` table with `kind = "datapack"`.

**The flow.** Request -> capability router (data-driven words) -> the build service's AI writes **typed spec files** `assets/datapack/<name>.json` (never raw Minecraft JSON) -> the service validates + emits them with the GENERATED copy of the TypeScript code for the build's exact version, bounded repairs, drop-not-ship -> the portal re-validates and re-emits (the service is not trusted), records a revision + a datapack asset -> (flag) delivery into `<level>/datapacks/` + `minecraft:reload` (or a restart for enchantments).

### 1. Files (`lib/cyrus/datapack/`)
| File | What |
|---|---|
| `spec.ts` | DataPackSpec v1 (Zod) + `validateDataPackSpec(json, { version, namespace })` -> `{ ok, spec, errors, warnings, checks }` (never throws) + `canonicalJson` + `needsRestart` |
| `datapack.v1.schema.json` | the portable contract (JSON Schema), generated (see below; a test fails while stale) |
| `versions.ts` | `dataPackFeatures(version)` (the verified per-version differences, below), `vanillaIds(kind, version)`, `isVanilla`, `missingIdReason` ("needs 1.21.11 or newer" / "was removed after 1.21.8") |
| `data/vanilla-ids.json` | ids ONLY (238 KB): items, blocks, entity types, enchantments, loot tables, advancements, recipes, item/block/entity/enchantment tags, loot function / condition / entry / number types, triggers, recipe serializers, enchantment effect components, mob effects, attributes, command roots, execute sub-commands, gamerules; grouped by a version bitmask. Generated by Mojang's data generator (`--reports --server`) from each pinned vanilla server jar on node-2 (sha256s in the file's `source`). No assets or content |
| `data/mcdoc-subset.json` | field tables derived from **vanilla-mcdoc** (SpyglassMC, MIT, commit `1528808766ccaaac10e64de002b05d3efc31a9a3`, attribution in the file): top-level keys, optional flags and `since`/`until` of every struct the emitters write |
| `mcdoc.ts` | resolves those tables per version (`dispatchFields`, `structFields`, `checkKeys`); outside the subset = null = not judged |
| `functions.ts` | the function SAFETY validator (allowlist, below) |
| `emit/{common,recipe,loot,advancement,enchantment,index}.ts` | per-version emitters; `buildDataPack(spec, ctx)` = validate -> emit -> static file check -> deterministic zip (`lib/cyrus/textures/zip.ts`: sorted entries, fixed timestamps) -> `{ zip, sha1, sha256, files, counts, apply: reload|restart, checks }` |
| `validate.ts` | `validatePackFiles(files, version)`: the static checker for emitted OR raw files (imports) |
| `route.ts` | `decideDataPackRoute` (build request), `routeWithDataPack` (router with the route switched on), `hasDatapacks`, flag `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO` |
| `sync.ts` | `checkReturnedDatapacks` (portal re-validation / re-emission, cross-pack duplicates) |
| `deliver.ts` | `planDataPackDelivery`, `rebuildForDelivery`, `deliverDataPack` (flag `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL`) |
| `import.ts` | `importDataPackZip`, `exportImported`, `checkRawResource` (edit/import library) |
| `service-entry.ts` | esbuild entry of the service copy |

Scripts: `scripts/cyrus/build-datapack-artifacts.ts [--check] [--out-dir DIR]` writes `services/modbuilder/datapack-spec.js` (bundled validator + emitter incl. zod and the id data, minified, 650 KB) and the JSON Schema; run it through `devhost run ... --out-dir /tank/nxeon-build/tmp/...` and copy back (devhost's next push deletes files written inside the node-2 copy). `scripts/cyrus/datapack-derive.py ids|mcdoc` re-derives the two data files on node-2 (see 8).

### 2. DataPackSpec v1
`{ schemaVersion: 1, name, description, resources: [1-128] }`; `name` = file name. Every resource lives in the project's reserved namespace (`id` is only the path; engine-core identifiers gained the kind `resource` for `nx_x:a/b/c`, recipes use the existing `recipe` kind). References are full ids: own ones must exist in the spec, vanilla ones must exist in the TARGET version's id lists, any other namespace is refused.
- **recipe**: `shaped` (pattern 1-3 x 1-3, key), `shapeless` (1-9), `smelting` / `blasting` / `smoking` / `campfire_cooking` (experience, cookingTime), `stonecutting`, `smithing_transform`. Ingredient = id, `#tag` or a list of alternatives. Result = vanilla item + count + optional `name` (`minecraft:item_name`) and `lore` (a data pack cannot add items). Not supported: `smithing_trim`, special recipes, `crafting_transmute`.
- **loot_table**: kind generic/chest/entity/block/fishing/gift; pools (rolls = number / uniform / binomial, bonusRolls), entries item / tag (expand) / loot_table / empty with weight, quality; **functions subset**: set_count, set_damage, enchant_randomly, enchant_with_levels, set_name, set_lore, set_enchantments, explosion_decay, furnace_smelt, looting_bonus (= enchanted_count_increase with looting); **conditions subset**: random_chance, killed_by_player, survives_explosion, match_tool (items / tag), weather.
- **advancement**: parent (own or vanilla), display (icon, title, description, frame, background from the five vanilla tabs, toast/chat/hidden), **criteria subset**: impossible, tick, inventory_changed, consume_item, player_killed_entity, recipe_unlocked, recipe_crafted; requirements all|any; rewards experience / loot / recipes / function.
- **tag**: registry item / block / entity_type / function / enchantment; own tags, or additions to an EXISTING vanilla tag (`replace` defaults false; `replace: true` on a vanilla tag is refused); function tags: own, `minecraft:load`, `minecraft:tick`.
- **function**: a list of commands (+ `runOn: load|tick`, merged into the vanilla function tags).
- **enchantment**: description, supportedItems / primaryItems (tag or items), exclusiveSet, weight, maxLevel, min/max cost, anvil cost, slots, value effects (`damage`, `damage_protection`, `knockback`, `armor_effectiveness`, `item_damage`, `mob_experience`, `block_experience`, `repair_with_xp`, `smash_damage_per_fallen_block`; add / multiply / set, linear per level). Supported because the format of this subset was **verified identical on all six versions** (vanilla sharpness/unbreaking compared on every jar, and the custom enchantment loaded and was applied to an item on all six real servers). Enchantments are registry content: `apply = "restart"`.
- Not in v1: worldgen (biomes, structures, dimensions: router warns), predicates / item modifiers as resources, vanilla loot-table or recipe overrides, macros.

### 3. Per-version differences (VERIFIED on the real jars, 2026-10-10)
Method: the vanilla data generator of each pinned server jar dumped the vanilla data pack; the same files were compared across versions, cross-checked with vanilla-mcdoc, then the emitted packs were booted (section 6).

| Difference | Versions | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Ingredients `{"item": id}` / `{"tag": id}` -> strings `"id"` / `"#tag"`; a list of alternatives may hold only item ids | 1.21.1 vs 1.21.2+ | vanilla `stick.json`, `fire_charge.json`, `netherite_sword_smithing.json`; mcdoc |
| Text in item components (`item_name`, `lore`) is a JSON **string** -> a text **object** | <=1.21.4 vs 1.21.5+ | vanilla `voluntary_exile.json` icon `minecraft:item_name` |
| Advancement background `minecraft:textures/gui/advancements/backgrounds/stone.png` -> `minecraft:gui/advancements/backgrounds/stone` | <=1.21.4 vs 1.21.5+ | vanilla `story/root.json` |
| `pack.mcmeta` `pack_format` -> `min_format` / `max_format` `[major, minor]` | <1.21.9 vs 1.21.9+ | mcdoc `pack.mcdoc`; registry formats 48 / 61 / 81 / 94.1 / 101.1 / 107.1 accepted by the real servers |
| Entity predicates `{"type": ...}` -> namespaced sub-predicates `{"minecraft:entity_type": ...}` | <26.2 vs 26.2 | vanilla `adventure/blowback.json`, `entities/zombie.json`; mcdoc `EntityPredicate` |
| Cooking results: single item (no count) -> item stack (count) | <26.1 vs 26.1+ | mcdoc `Smelting`; the validator refuses count > 1 before 26.1 |
| `smithing_transform.group` removed; `category` optional (26.2 vanilla drops it from many recipes) | 26.1+ / 26.2 | mcdoc; vanilla 26.2 recipes |
| Advancement icons: vanilla writes `count: 1` before 26.1, omits it after (both load; we mirror vanilla) | 26.1 | vanilla advancements |
| Loot `loot_table` entries reference by `value` (not `name`); tag entries need `expand` before 26.3 | all | mcdoc |
| Gamerules camelCase -> snake_case (`keepInventory` -> `keep_inventory`) | <=1.21.8 vs 1.21.11+ | `commands.json` of each jar |
| Item tag `#minecraft:enchantable/sword` removed, `#minecraft:enchantable/melee_weapon` added | 1.21.11 | vanilla tags (the validator caught it on the showcase) |
| Commands `rotate` (1.21.4+), `dialog`, `version`, `waypoint`, `test` (1.21.8+), `stopwatch`, `fetchprofile` (1.21.11+), `swing`, `unpublish` (26.x) | per version | `commands.json` |

### 4. Validation (quality-bar style checks: pass / warn / fail / not_run)
Spec checks: `schema`, `namespace`, `vanilla_ids`, `references`, `version_features`, `limits`, `function_safety`. File checks on the emitted (or imported) files: `mcmeta`, `mcdoc_fields` (unknown / missing keys per version), `value_shapes` (the format changes above), `emitted_ids` (recipe types, loot function / condition / entry types, triggers, items), `emitted_functions`, `not_checked` (resources outside the subset: listed, kept, never judged). The same report is stored with every datapack asset.

**Function allowlist** (`functions.ts`; functions run as the server at `function-permission-level`, 2 by default, up to 4 on some hosts). Allowed roots: advancement, attribute, bossbar, clear, clone, damage, data, dialog, effect, enchant, execute, experience/xp, fill, fillbiome, forceload, function, gamemode, gamerule, give, item, kill, list, locate, loot, me, msg/tell/w, particle, place, playsound, random, recipe, return, ride, rotate, say, schedule, scoreboard, setblock, spawnpoint, spectate, spreadplayers, stopsound, stopwatch, summon, swing, tag, team, teammsg/tm, teleport/tp, tellraw, time, title, trigger, waypoint, weather, worldborder; each must also exist in the target version's real command tree. Refused: op, deop, ban, ban-ip, banlist, pardon, pardon-ip, kick, whitelist, stop, save-off/on/all, reload, publish/unpublish, transfer, difficulty, defaultgamemode, setidletimeout, setworldspawn, seed, tick, debug, jfr, perf, test, fetchprofile, datapack, version, every namespaced root (`minecraft:op`, `bukkit:...`, plugin commands such as `lp`), macros (`$` lines, `function ... with`), `run_command` click actions, Command NBT, command / structure / jigsaw blocks, command-block minecarts and debug sticks anywhere, creative mode, `kill @e` without a type/tag/team/name/limit filter (`kill @a` warns), gamerules outside a gameplay list (both name styles). `execute ... run` and `return run` are unwrapped and checked to the end (nesting <= 12). Call graph over function / `execute if function` / function tags: no recursion, depth <= 8, calls only to this pack's own functions. Limits: 64 functions, 256 commands per function, 2048 commands and 256 KB per pack, 2000 chars per line, no line breaks, 64 commands per tick (tick functions and everything they call), 16 schedule commands (>= 1 tick, no `append` from tick functions), 4 `forceload add` (one chunk each). A summon in a tick function warns. Adversarial corpus: `test/fixtures/cyrus-datapack/function-corpus.json` (61 cases).

### 5. Router, build service, portal
- **Router** (`adapters/minecraft.ts`, `engine-core/router.ts`): rules `datapack_recipe`, `datapack_loot`, `datapack_advancement`, `datapack_tag`, `datapack_function`, `datapack_enchantment`, `datapack_content` route to `dataPack` with limits (vanilla items only; function allowlist; enchantments need a restart; client-visible looks still need a resource pack); `worldgen` is now a `warn` ("not built yet; needs a restart"). The adapter keeps `dataPack` as `planned`; `RouteOptions.routesOn` lets the host switch a planned route on (`routeWithDataPack` does it under the flag), so `plugin+dataPack` becomes buildable only where enabled. "Creepers drop diamonds" stays a plugin (vanilla loot overrides are not in v1).
- **Build request** (`lib/cyrus/assets/request.ts`, one line in `lib/modbuilder/create.ts`): with the flag on, matched words, `assets: ["datapack"]` or a base build that has data packs give `service.assets.datapack = true` and a project namespace (no plan lookup); `ModBuild.cyrus.assets.datapack = { route, matched, limits }`; a version without an emitter (26.3) gets a notice and no route. Flag off: nothing decided, nothing recorded.
- **Build service** (`services/modbuilder/{datapacks.js,datapack-spec.js,datapack-example.json,prompts.js,server.js,textures.js}`): `assets.datapack` parsed (non-boolean = 400; switched off with a note where the bundle has no emitter for the version); the `DATA PACK` section is appended to the system prompt only when routed (fixed text, caches per version; the namespace is in the user turn); allow-list `assets/datapack/<name>.json` (max 4); a change build without the route keeps the base's specs byte for byte; every asset round runs `checkWorkspaceDatapacks` (the generated `buildDataPack` for the exact version + cross-file duplicates; HARD problems go back as `repair-asset`, bounded by `MB_MAX_ASSET_REPAIRS`, then the spec is dropped with a customer-visible limitation); `assetResult.datapacks: [{ name, path, sha256, spec, pack: { sha256, bytes, format, counts, apply, emitter }, checks, warnings }]`, `datapackPromptVersion` `mb-datapack-2026-10-10.1`; `/health` lists `datapack`. Data pack builds are never deduped. The service image needs the three new files.
- **Portal sync** (`lib/cyrus/assets/sync.ts` + `datapack/sync.ts`): every returned spec is re-validated and re-emitted for `ModBuild.mcVersion`; failures and cross-pack duplicates are dropped; the same single revision of the build gets `assets/datapack/<name>.json` (role `asset`, spec sha256) and `datapack/<name>-<version>.zip` (role `dataPack`, zip sha256); one `CyrusProjectAsset` per pack (`kind datapack`, mime `application/vnd.nxeon.datapack-spec+json`, provenance = spec, version, format, pack sha256/sha1, counts, apply, checks, `serviceAgreed`); `MbAssets.datapacks`. Idempotent (revision by modBuildId, content-addressed assets). **No hosting**: data packs never go to clients, and the emitter is deterministic, so delivery rebuilds the zip from the stored spec and checks the recorded sha256 (`rebuildForDelivery`); nothing is public.
- **Delivery** (`datapack/deliver.ts`, flag `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL`): one file `<level>/datapacks/nxeon-<namespace>-<name>.zip` placed through a `MemberPlacer` (production: `engineMemberPlacer`, the Mods engine, staged writes, state file), then `minecraft:reload` over the console for reloadable content, or `restartRequired` for enchantments. **Remaining steps (not wired)**: (1) a worker job after the jar install that loads the build's datapack assets, `rebuildForDelivery`, and calls `deliverDataPack` with `engineMemberPlacer` + the server's level name + an RCON/console `runConsole`; (2) removal = the placer's `remove` + reload when a mod is uninstalled; (3) the NxLabs page line; (4) a real-server check of `minecraft:reload` discovering a NEW pack file (Test Flight reserves `reload`; boot discovery and `datapack disable/enable` were verified).

### 6. Import / edit (`datapack/import.ts`, a library for the import agent)
`importDataPackZip(buf)` uses the bounded zip reader (5000 entries, 1 MB per entry, 32 MB total, ratio cap, CRC; unsafe names reported, never extracted; a single top folder is stripped) and converts what fits the subset for the pack's main namespace (recipes, loot tables, advancements, tags incl. vanilla-tag additions, functions; the Cyrus function header is recognised). Everything else stays a RAW resource with its bytes and a reason (enchantments, worldgen, predicates, structures, vanilla overrides, unknown fields or types, pack.png). `exportImported(imp, { spec?, rawEdits? }, { version, retarget? })` writes unchanged converted resources with their ORIGINAL bytes (exact round trip), re-emits edited ones for the version, keeps every raw file (edited ones replaced as text) and returns the file report; `checkRawResource` is the editor's live check.

### 7. Tests and real runs
- RAN on devhost: `test/cyrus-datapack.test.ts` (92 pure: feature matrix, id drift, mcdoc tables, the showcase valid on all six versions with every check passing, 18 broken-spec codes, golden zip hashes per version = the flown zips, determinism, each per-version difference, raw broken pack + a 1.21.1 pack checked for 26.2, the 61-case function corpus, artifacts current, TS == generated JS on 71 shared inputs (validation results and pack bytes), prompt section, routing, not-plan-gated build request, import round trips + third-party pack + hostile zip, delivery off/on/restart/disabled, rebuild, sync with injected deps). `test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts` (20, 4 new: routed build with section + namespace + Read/Write/Edit, service pack bytes == TypeScript; denied command -> one repair; unknown item -> 2 repairs then dropped; not routed -> file removed, change keeps the spec, malformed flag 400). Whole Cyrus + modbuilder suite 995/995. `tsc` clean.
- RAN on the throwaway DB (`devhost db push`, then `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DB_TEST=1 npx tsx --test test/cyrus-datapack-db.test.ts`): 2/2 (free account gets the route with a real project and no plan row; flag off creates nothing; sync = 1 revision with the dataPack role, 1 datapack asset, idempotent on re-sync and 3 concurrent syncs; the stored asset rebuilds the exact zip).
- RAN REAL on node-2 through Test Flight, one flight at a time (`devhost run -- npx tsx test/cyrus-datapack-real.ts all --local`; raw: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/datapack-r2-flights-2026-10-10.json` and, a second complete run on the final code with identical results, `datapack-r2-flights-final-2026-10-10.json`): the showcase (6 recipes incl. smithing, 6 loot tables, 3 advancements, 6 tags incl. a vanilla-tag addition and a function tag, 5 functions with load/tick, 1 enchantment) on every pinned version. Each flight: `datapack list enabled` shows `file/cyrus_showcase.zip`; startup log clean (0 hits); load tag ran (`#loaded has 1`), tick tag runs, `function nx_dpstud10:hello` -> `#hello has 143` (helper call + execute chain), the function tag runs; `loot spawn` of the frost sword -> `data get` shows `nx_dpstud10:frostbite` and the custom name; tag-entry, treasure and extras tables drop items; `execute if block ... #nx_dpstud10:shiny` and `execute if entity @e[type=#nx_dpstud10:pals]` pass; `datapack disable` -> the function is unknown, `datapack enable` -> it runs again (the reload path); the server log's "Loaded N recipes / advancements" equals vanilla + ours exactly (so every recipe and advancement loaded).

| Version | Paper / JDK | Result | Recipes loaded (vanilla + 6) | Advancements (vanilla + 3) | Boot | Peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.21.1 | b133 / 21 | passed | 1296 = 1290 + 6 | 1402 = 1399 + 3 | 16.1 s | 1031 MB |

## Cyrus Test Flight (R0)

"Test Flight lite" (2026-10-10, branch `feature/cyrus-r0`, **not wired into the build path, nothing deployed**): boot ONE throwaway real Paper server for one registry version on node-2, load the given plugin jars / datapacks, run the checks, tear it down, return a JSON report. Master plan 4.6.

**Files**
- `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight/runner.js`: the runner (plain Node, no deps; runs on node-2 as root). `node runner.js run <resolved-spec.json>` prints the report JSON; `node runner.js setup 21|25` fetches + verifies a pinned JDK.
- `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight/lib.js`: its pure helpers (log matchers + default ignores, plugin.yml-from-jar reader, `plugins` reply parser, RCON wire format, server.properties, resolved-spec validation).
- `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight/fixtures/`: `hello` (positive control, `/tfhello`), `broken` (throws in onEnable), `datapack-tf_smoke` (one function), `build.sh` (javac `--release N -proc:none` against a classpath file + reproducible `jar --date`, same as the build service).
- `lib/cyrus/testflight/types.ts` (spec/report types), `spec.ts` (`validateSpec`, `resolveSpec`, `requiredStages`; fail closed on the registry), `summary.ts` (`summarize`, `mergeSummaries`, `describe`), `client.ts` (`runTestFlight`, `sshRemote`, injectable `Remote`).
- Spec extras (added with pack delivery): `files` (small text files placed under `plugins/` before boot, max 16 x 64 KB) and per-RCON-check `writeFile` / `waitMs` (replace a file, optionally wait up to 30 s, then send the command), so a plugin's config reload can be tested. Both validators (`spec.ts`, `lib.js`) confine paths to `plugins/<plain segments>`.
- Tests: `test/cyrus-testflight.test.ts` (pure, 24 tests), `test/cyrus-testflight-real.ts` (real node-2 runs, run by hand: `tsx test/cyrus-testflight-real.ts all --out r.json`).
- Registry: `paperBuild`/`paperServerSha256` now also pin the **server** jar for 1.21.11 (build 132, Fill STABLE). A version without a server pin cannot be test-flown (1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8 and 26.3 today).

**Checks, in order** (each `pass` / `fail` / `not_run` with evidence lines; a check never passes unless it ran):
1. `boot_done`: a `Done (Xs)!` line within `bootSec` (default 180).
2. `plugins_enabled`: per plugin (name read from the jar's plugin.yml / paper-plugin.yml): log has `Enabling <name> v`, no `Error occurred while enabling`, no `Disabling <name>` before stop, and the RCON `plugins` listing shows it green (red = disabled = fail).
3. `startup_log_clean`: default matchers (ERROR/FATAL level, exception headers, enable/load errors, datapack load errors) over the log up to the Done line. Spec `logMatchers` replace them (an empty list is refused), `logIgnore` adds ignores. The two built-in ignores cover only noise the sandbox itself causes (no internet: Mojang public-key fetch, Paper version fetch); ignored lines are counted in the evidence.
4. `rcon_checks`: spec commands with `expect`/`expectNot` substrings (colour codes stripped), plus an automatic `datapack list enabled` check per datapack. stop/restart/op/deop/reload are reserved.
5. `clean_stop`: `stop` over RCON (stdin fallback), exit code 0 within `stopSec`, no matcher hits during shutdown.
6. `no_leaks`: our java PID gone, no process anywhere carrying this run's `-Dnxeon.testflight.run=<runId>` marker, no listening port in the reserved range (checked inside the netns and on the host).

**Verdict** (`summary.ts`, pure): required stages come from the spec we sent (boot, log, stop, leaks always; plugins if any plugin; rcon if any command or datapack; plus `requireStages`), not from the runner's flags. Any required fail = `failed`; any required stage missing / `not_run` / "pass" with no evidence = `incomplete`; `busy` and `error` reports are never success. `success` is true only for `passed`.

**Safety on node-2** (shared build host): one flight at a time (`flock -n` on `TF_ROOT/testflight.lock`; a second caller gets `status: "busy"` immediately, exit 75); the server runs in a private network namespace (`unshare --net`, loopback only: no internet, cannot reach or collide with host ports) as uid/gid 65534 with `no_new_privs`, `nice 10`, `-Xmx1g` max, SerialGC, 2 visible CPUs, an RSS watchdog (default 1800 MB) and a hard timeout (runner `totalSec` default 420 + an outer `timeout -s KILL`); kills are only ever by exact PID after re-checking the marker in `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`; the run dir and the upload inbox are always removed. Paper jars are fetched from the Fill API only when Fill's sha256 equals the registry pin, then pre-patched once (`paperclip.patchonly`, `bundlerRepoDir`) into a root-owned cache the server cannot write. Plugin jars are re-hashed on node-2 against the hash the invoker computed.

**node-2 layout** (`TF_ROOT=/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/testflight`, about 1.5 GB): `jdk/21` (Temurin 21.0.12.1+1, sha256 ce79869e...bcfaee94) and `jdk/25` (Temurin 25.0.4.1+1, sha256 dbb69839...215cf41e), both checked against the Adoptium API; `dl/` (tarballs by sha256); `paper/<sha256>/` (server jar + pre-patched libraries); `runner/` (the invoker pushes `runner.js`/`lib.js` whenever their hash differs from the repo); `runs/` (per-flight dirs, removed); `inbox/` (uploads, removed; `inbox/fx` holds the fixture jars); `reports/<runId>.json`; `classpath/1.21.11.txt` (+ `.sha256`) and `gradle-home/` from resolving the 1.21.11 compile classpath with the template (Gradle 8.14.3 on JDK 21, 24.7 s, 850 MB peak).

**Measured on node-2 (2026-10-10, RAN)**, Done-line wall time from JVM spawn and peak RSS (VmHWM), tiny flat world, `-Xmx1g`:

| Version | JDK | Plugin | Boot (wall) | Paper "Done" | Peak RSS | Whole flight (runner) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 26.2 b133 | 25 | HelloR0 + datapack | 10.6 s | 9.2 s | 803 MB | 13.5 s |
| 26.2 b133 | 25 | TfBroken | 10.6 s | 9.3 s | 762 MB | 12.4 s |
| 26.1.2 b74 | 25 | none | 10.4-10.8 s | 9.3-9.4 s | 722-729 MB | 12.2-16.8 s |
| 1.21.11 b132 | 21 | TfHello + datapack | 18.0 s | 16.6 s | 878 MB | 20.4 s |

One-off per Paper jar: download + pre-patch about 5 s. End to end from the primary over ssh adds about 5-10 s (each ssh connection to node-2 costs about 2.2 s; the invoker uses two: runner hash check, then one call that uploads a tar of artifacts + spec and runs the flight). The research estimate (20-45 s boot, 1.0-1.5 GB) was pessimistic: plan for about 20 s and 1 GB per flight. Capacity: one flight at a time by design, so about 3 flights a minute on 26.x and 2 on 1.21.11, using about 1 GB RAM and up to 2 cores while it runs.

**Results of the real runs (RAN)**: HelloR0 on 26.2 passed all 6 checks (`/hellor0` answered, `function tf:hello` ran, `file/tf_smoke` enabled); TfBroken on 26.2 failed `plugins_enabled` and `startup_log_clean` with the enable-error line, the `IllegalStateException` header and the red `plugins` entry as evidence (boot/stop/leaks still pass); TfHello compiled with JDK 21 `--release 21` against the template-resolved 1.21.11 classpath passed all 6 on Paper 1.21.11; a second flight started 4 s into another came back `busy` with every check `not_run` while the first passed. After the runs: no process with the marker, no port in 47100-47199, empty `runs/` and inbox (verified). An earlier 1.21.11 run correctly FAILED its log check because `-Dcom.mojang.eula.agree` logs at ERROR level on 1.21.11; the flag was removed (eula.txt is written instead).

**NOT RUN / not covered**: no player or bot joins (PlayerJoin listeners, GUIs, the resource-pack prompt are untested; `resourcePack` is only written to server.properties and reported `exercised: false`); no MockBukkit or Mineflayer scenarios; Paper 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8 and 26.3 have no server pin; the runner runs as root on node-2 and only the server drops privileges (no container/cgroup limits; a cgroup memory cap via systemd-run would be the next hardening step).

**Hand-off: how the portal/worker would call it** (not wired yet): from a worker job (never a request handler; a flight takes 15-30 s), after a successful build: `const { summary, report } = await runTestFlight({ version, plugins: [{ localPath: jarPath, sha256 }], datapacks, rcon: [{ command: "plugins", expect: [pluginName] }, ...specChecks] })`. Store `report` (it carries the runner hash, JDK + Paper sha256s, artifact sha256s) next to the build's engine-release record, and show `describe(summary)`; only `summary.success` may show a "booted on Paper X" badge. On `busy`, requeue with backoff (do not run in parallel). Run it from the primary (the worker host) via `sshRemote()`; the build VM 88001 is not involved. For a version matrix, run sequentially and combine with `mergeSummaries`.

**Owner actions**: none to deploy. Decide later (a) whether to gate publishing on `summary.success` once wired, (b) whether to pin Paper server builds for 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8 so they can be test-flown, (c) whether to add cgroup limits (systemd-run scope) on node-2 for the flight. Cleanup when no longer needed: `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/testflight` (about 1.5 GB) and `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/r0-26x` (about 2 GB, the 26.x lane probe, still used as the source of the HelloR0 fixture jar and the 26.2 classpath).


### 2. Conflict engine (`lib/cyrus/conflicts/`, pure + deterministic)
`detectConflicts(mods: ModEntry[], ctx)` -> `{ findings, counts, blocking, notChecked }`. A `ModEntry` is a plugin (descriptor + bytecode summary + jar flags), datapack index or resource-pack index, origin `server` or `candidate`, with its Cyrus namespace when built by Cyrus. Mods are sorted first; a finding id is a hash of class + subject + mods (stable, used to acknowledge a warning). Data a class needs but does not have goes to `notChecked` (never reported as clean). `normalize.ts` turns an inventory or candidate jars into entries.

| Class | Severity | Resolution suggested |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin.duplicate_name` | blocking | remove_one |
| `plugin.duplicate_main` (different names) | warn | remove_one |
| `command.label_collision` (plugin.yml label or Brigadier root) / `command.alias_collision` | warn / info | alias_rewrite proposal for a Cyrus mod (`/<4 ns chars><label>`, rebuild needed), else user decision |
| `command.vanilla_override` | warn (vanilla) / info (platform commands) | alias_rewrite (Cyrus) or none |
| `permission.duplicate`, `permission.default_mismatch` | warn | reserved_namespace (Cyrus) / user decision |
| `dependency.missing` (depend / softdepend) | blocking / info | upgrade_or_replace (add the dependency) |
| `dependency.cycle` (hard) / `dependency.loadbefore_cycle` | blocking / warn | user decision / load_order |
| `platform.api_version` (api-version newer than the server), `platform.java` (class major), `platform.folia` (Folia without folia-supported; warn: declares Folia but uses BukkitScheduler), `platform.item_model_version` (item models before 1.21.4) | blocking (Folia scheduler: warn) | upgrade_or_replace |
| `event.overlap` (>= 2 plugins change/cancel the same event at the same priority), `event.monitor_mutation` | warn | load_order |
| `key.namespacedkey`, `item.item_model`, `recipe.key`, `item.custom_model_data` | warn | reserved_namespace (Cyrus) / user decision |
| `key.namespace_foreign` (a Cyrus mod uses another project's `nx_` namespace) | warn | reserved_namespace |
| `resource.single_owner` | blocking for economy/permission providers, warn for chat renderer, tab list, sidebar, world rules, join/quit messages | user decision |
| `datapack.tag_replace`, `datapack.vanilla_override` (same `minecraft:` id twice; one override = info), `datapack.id_collision`, `datapack.function_tag_order` (#minecraft:load/tick) | warn / warn / warn / info | merge proposal / stacking_order / reserved_namespace / stacking_order (auto) |
| `rp.whole_file` (same path, different bytes: models, blockstates, items, textures...) | warn | stacking_order (auto: higher member wins, the same as Pack Loader stacking) |
| `rp.shader` | warn | user decision (never merged) |
| `rp.font_codepoint` | warn | reserved_namespace (Cyrus glyph blocks) / user decision |
| `rp.sounds_json`, `sound.key` (same custom event, different content) | warn (info when events are disjoint) | merge (auto) |
| `sound.vanilla_replace` (`minecraft` sounds.json event; `replace: true`) | warn (info without replace) | none (review) |
| `rp.lang`, `rp.atlas` | info | merge (auto) |
| `rp.existing_owner` (server already has a pack owner and we add a pack) | warn | user decision |
| `budget.display_entities`, `budget.tasks`, `budget.pack_size` (declared budgets, else bytecode sites marked "estimated") | warn (pack size in a Mod Pack: blocking) | user decision / remove_one |
| `policy.server_jar`, `safety.jar_flags` | blocking in a Mod Pack, warn on a server | remove_one |

pack.mcmeta and pack.png are not conflicts (the composer writes its own pack.mcmeta from the version registry).

**Merges** (`merge.ts`, inputs lowest priority first): `mergeSoundsJson` (events unioned, sounds concatenated + deduped in canonical order; a later `replace:true` drops lower sounds, reported; a lower `replace:true` plus a later plain contribution is reported as order-dependent), `mergeLang` (later wins, reported), `mergeTag` (exact Minecraft stacking: replace clears lower values, reported), `mergeAtlas` (sources concatenated), `mergeFont` (providers concatenated, codepoint overlaps reported), `mergeWholeFile` (identical collapses, else top wins, reported). Laws tested with 300 seeded cases each: idempotent (`merge([a,a]) == merge([a])`, `merge([merge(xs)]) == merge(xs)`), no key loss (tags: every value unless a reported replace), order-stable whenever no conflict is reported, deterministic bytes. `resourcepack.ts composeResourcePacks` builds one pack (or says `unmergeable` when two inputs ship shaders).

**Weld / Beet evaluation (MASTER-PLAN 4.8): documented, not installed.** Beet 0.119.1 is MIT on PyPI but now requires Python >= 3.14; the primary and node-2 run 3.13.5, so it is not usable without a separate Python. `smithed` 0.19.0 (Weld) declares no licence in its PyPI metadata (the repository says MIT, per the research: UNVERIFIED here), needs beet + mecha + pydantic, and its per-file merge rules were not documented in what was read. Both would run as an offline subprocess on a build host. Decision: the format-aware merges above are small, pure and law-tested in TypeScript; revisit Weld behind golden tests only if datapack merging (rewriting member datapacks) becomes a requirement.

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there

I'm thinking through how custom dimensions get generated and whether spawn chunks stay loaded in Paper 1.21, then planning to verify behavior by forceloading chunks in the custom dimension directly.

I need to be careful about which commands actually work without loaded chunks: `locate biome` just samples the biome source so it's safe, but `locate structure` can trigger partial generation up to structure-start status, and `place structure` likely checks that the target chunks are loaded first, throwing an error otherwise. So the test plan needs to forceload the relevant chunks before attempting a `place structure` call.

I'm also considering how to verify generation finished — `execute if loaded` seems like the cleanest check since it confirms the chunk is fully loaded without depending on world-specific terrain assumptions, and it's been available since 1.19.4 alongside `execute positioned over`.

Then I could read the marker's position data to get the surface height, and chain locate commands for biomes within the dimension context.

For timing, boot overhead mainly comes from dimension spawn chunk generation, though only overworld prepares spawn chunks by default in newer versions, and with 1GB heap, generating a few chunks of noise should still be manageable.

For structures, I'd use a structure_set with random_spread restricted to the custom biome, then locate it with a dimension-scoped locate structure command.

Keeping spacing small for quick placement, I'd use jigsaw structures with a single-piece template_pool entry sized to one, anchored at a fixed height and projected onto the heightmap — the standard village-style approach, accounting for how jigsaw structure fields differ slightly across 1.20.5+ and 1.21.x versions.

use ::java::util::color::StringRGB
use ::java::util::particle::Particle
use ::java::util::WeightedList
use ::java::util::FlatWeightedList
use super::attribute::PositionalEnvironmentAttributeMap
use super::CarveStep

use super::carver::CarverListRef

use super::surface_builder::ConfiguredSurfaceBuilderRef
use super::IntProvider
use super::super::util::SoundEventRef

dispatch minecraft:resource["worldgen/biome"] to struct Biome {
	#[since="1.21.11"]
	attributes?: PositionalEnvironmentAttributeMap,
	#[until="1.19"]
	category: BiomeCategory,
	/// Raises or lowers the terrain. Positive values are considered land and negative are oceans.
	#[until="1.18"]
	depth: float,
	/// Vertically stretches the terrain. Lower values produce flatter terrain.
	#[until="1.18"]
	scale: float,
	temperature: float,
	downfall: float,
	#[until="1.19.4"]
	precipitation: Precipitation,
	#[since="1.19.4"]
	has_precipitation: boolean,
	temperature_modifier?: TemperatureModifier,
	/// If true, the world spawn will be preferred in this biome.
	#[until="1.18"]
	player_spawn_friendly?: boolean,
	effects: BiomeEffects,
	#[until="1.18"]
	surface_builder: ConfiguredSurfaceBuilderRef,
	#[until="1.18"]
	starts: [StructureRef],
	#[until="26.3"]
	...NaturalMobSpawns,
	carvers: (
		#[until="1.21.2"] struct CarversPerStep {
			[CarveStep]: (
				#[until="1.18.2"] [CarverRef] |
				#[since="1.18.2"] CarverListRef |
			),
		} |
		#[since="1.21.2"] CarverListRef |
	),
	features: (
		#[until="1.18"] [[ConfiguredFeatureRef]] @ ..10 |
		#[since="1.18"] [(
			[PlacedFeatureRef] |
			#[since="1.18.2"] #[id(registry="worldgen/placed_feature",tags="required")] string |
		)] @ ..11 |
	),
}

enum (string) BiomeCategory {
	Beach = "beach",
	Desert = "desert",
	ExtremeHills = "extreme_hills",
	Forest = "forest",
	Icy = "icy",
	Jungle = "jungle",
	Mesa = "mesa",
	#[since="1.18"] Mountain = "mountain",
	Mushroom = "mushroom",
	Nether = "nether",
	None = "none",
	Ocean = "ocean",
	Plains = "plains",
	River = "river",
	Savanna = "savanna",
	Swamp = "swamp",
	Taiga = "taiga",
	TheEnd = "the_end",
	#[since="1.17"] Underground = "underground",
}

enum(string) Precipitation {
	None = "none",
	Rain = "rain",
	Snow = "snow",
}

enum(string) TemperatureModifier {
	None = "none",
	Frozen = "frozen",
}

struct BiomeEffects {
	#[until="1.21.11"]
	sky_color: #[color="composite_rgb"] int,
	#[until="1.21.11"]
	fog_color: #[color="composite_rgb"] int,
	water_color: (
		#[until="1.21.11"] #[color="composite_rgb"] int |
		#[since="1.21.11"] StringRGB |
	),
	#[until="1.21.11"]
	water_fog_color: #[color="composite_rgb"] int,
	grass_color?: (
		#[until="1.21.11"] #[color="composite_rgb"] int |
		#[since="1.21.11"] StringRGB |
	),
	foliage_color?: (
		#[until="1.21.11"] #[color="composite_rgb"] int |
		#[since="1.21.11"] StringRGB |
	),
	#[since="1.21.5"]
	dry_foliage_color?: (
		#[until="1.21.11"] #[color="composite_rgb"] int |
		#[since="1.21.11"] StringRGB |
	),
	grass_color_modifier?: GrassColorModifier,
	#[until="1.21.11"]
	ambient_sound?: SoundEventRef,
	#[until="1.21.11"]
	mood_sound?: struct MoodSound {
		sound: SoundEventRef,
		tick_delay: int,
		block_search_extent: int,
		offset: float,
	},
	#[until="1.21.11"]
	additions_sound?: struct BiomeSoundAdditions {
		sound: SoundEventRef,
		tick_chance: float @ 0..1,
	},
	#[until="1.21.11"]
	music?: (
		#[until="1.21.4"] BiomeMusic |
		#[since="1.21.4"] WeightedList<BiomeMusic> |
	),
	/// The volume of the music in this biome. Defaults to 1.
	/// The game will smoothly transition between the current music volume and the new volume when entering the biome.
	#[since="1.21.4"] #[until="1.21.11"]
	music_volume?: float,
	#[until="1.21.11"]
	particle?: struct BiomeParticle {
		options: Particle,
		probability: float @ 0..1,
	},
}

enum(string) GrassColorModifier {
	None = "none",
	/// Grass color will be average of the base color and `#28340a`.
	DarkForest = "dark_forest",

	/// The base color is ignored.
	Swamp = "swamp",
}

struct BiomeMusic {
	sound: SoundEventRef,
	min_delay: int @ 0..,
	max_delay: int @ 0..,
	#[until="1.21.11"] ...struct {
		replace_current_music: boolean,
	},
	#[since="1.21.11"] ...struct {
		/// Defaults to `false`.
		replace_current_music?: boolean,
	},
}

enum(string) MobCategory {
	Monster = "monster",
	Creature = "creature",
	Ambient = "ambient",
	#[since="1.18"] Axolotls = "axolotls",
	#[since="1.17"] UndergroundWaterCreature = "underground_water_creature",
	WaterCreature = "water_creature",
	WaterAmbient = "water_ambient",
	Misc = "misc",
}

struct NaturalMobSpawns {
	#[until="26.3"]
	creature_spawn_probability?: float @ 0..0.9999999,
	#[until="26.3"]
	spawners: SpawnerDataMap,
	#[since="26.3"]
	spawns_by_category: SpawnerDataMap,
	spawn_costs: struct {
		[#[id="entity"] string]: MobSpawnCost,
	},
}

struct SpawnerDataMap {
	[MobCategory]: FlatWeightedList<SpawnerData>,
}

struct SpawnerData {
	type: #[id="entity_type"] string,
	#[until="26.3"]
	minCount: int,
	#[until="26.3"]
	maxCount: int,
	#[since="26.3"]
	count: IntProvider<int>,
}

struct MobSpawnCost {
	energy_budget: double,
	charge: double,
}

content.thinking:
I should trust mcdoc's claim that music became a WeightedList starting in 1.21.4, verifying against vanilla's 1.21.4 cherry_grove data since 26.3 is out of scope. This requires a lot of research, so I need to tightly scope the subset and figure out whether the DataPackSpec schema version needs to change.

Keeping v1 specs valid byte-for-byte means I can extend the ResourceSchema union with new worldgen resource kinds without breaking existing golden-hash tests, even though the generated JSON Schema file changes. But I need gating: worldgen resources should only validate when a worldgen flag is explicitly passed into validateDataPackSpec, failing closed with a "worldgen_off" error otherwise. The portal and sync paths need to pass this flag consistently based on whether worldgen is actually enabled for that build.

Now I'm working out the shape of the new resource kinds themselves — a `dimension_type` schema built around presets with knobs like height, ambient light, skylight/ceiling flags, spawn settings, and dimension effects, plus a `dimension` schema referencing a dimension type and a noise-based generator settings preset. I need to check how the dimension_type format has shifted across Minecraft versions before locking in the field list.

For the generator, I'm restricting biome sources to fixed, checkerboard, or multi_noise variants (with climate parameters), or a flat generator with layered blocks, while keeping noise settings limited to vanilla presets only to avoid unsafe custom noise configs — I still need to pin down valid height ranges and multiples-of-16 constraints for dimension height.

I also need to validate that each dimension_type's min_y/height range properly contains the chosen noise preset's vertical range, so I'll hardcode known preset ranges (overworld, nether, end, caves, floating_islands) and check compatibility, plus estimate a relative generation cost for each generator type.

For the biome schema, I'm laying out fields for temperature, downfall, precipitation, color settings (sky, fog, water, grass, foliage), sound events (music, ambient, mood, additions), and particle effects limited to a small preset list of simple particle types.

I also need to account for spawners capped at 16 entries, feature steps as an ordered list of 11 phases with references capped at 24, and carver lists limited to known vanilla carver ids like cave, canyon, cave_extra_underground, and nether_cave — and I should check the registries file for valid sound event ids.

Since I don't have detailed mob category data, I'll rely on a curated allowlist of roughly 40 spawnable mobs per category rather than trying to derive spawn eligibility from entity type alone, excluding things like ender_dragon, wither, player, and item frames. For configured features, I'm documenting the "ore" kind with target blocks like stone, deepslate, netherrack, end_stone, or block tags.

Trees are trickier since trunk and foliage placers vary across versions, so I'm sketching a simplified "tree" option with log/leaf blocks, height and radius ranges rather than exposing the full vanilla complexity. I'm also drafting a "patch" kind for random_patch/flower-style features with plant blocks, try counts, and spread values.

For "lake," I'm mapping it to the minecraft:lake feature config with fluid and barrier state providers, noting it's deprecated but still present; I'm deciding to skip disk and block_column for now and just keep ore, tree, patch, lake, and placement as the supported set.

I also realize biome feature lists can reference vanilla placed features directly, like minecraft:trees_plains, which means I should allow vanilla placed feature refs in biome feature lists validated against a version id list. For placed_feature, I'm sketching its schema: a feature reference plus a placement list with modifiers like count, rarity_filter, in_square, height_range, biome, and heightmap.

For structure_template, I'm defining a block layout spec with size limits (48 cubed), a palette mapping single characters to blocks with up to 32 entries, and layers made of row strings, with spaces or dots meaning void. I'm figuring out how this compiles into NBT data with a DataVersion field.

I need to track down the correct DataVersion per Minecraft version, likely pulling "world_version" from the server jar's version.json, and I'm setting practical caps like a max block count (32768 non-void blocks) to stay under NBT size limits while keeping structures usable.

For origin, I'm deciding it should map to vertical offset only — origin.y translates to a negative absolute start_height for a jigsaw piece using project_start_to_heightmap, sinking the structure so its anchor sits at the surface. The x/z components of origin can be ignored since jigsaw piece placement is already handled by chunk positioning.

I'm also considering whether to support chests with loot tables in the palette, letting a block entry reference a loot table that gets written into block NBT with a LootTable field and the chest's block id — a nice connective feature worth including since it's cheap to add.

I should maintain a deny list for dangerous palette blocks like command blocks, structure blocks, jigsaw, spawners, TNT, and portal blocks, possibly reusing an existing deny list from functions.ts, while thinking about whether to validate block state properties against the blocks.json report since it contains the allowed property values per block.

I could derive a compact property table by deduping common property signatures across ~1100 blocks rather than storing full data per block, keeping the size to roughly 30-50KB, which seems like a reasonable tradeoff for the bundle. I'm also sketching out the structure field schema, covering jigsaw_single kind with template references, biome tags, and step values.

For structure_sets, I need to enforce caps like minimum spacing of 4, max 4 structures per set, and max 8 sets, while limiting structures to the mod's own biomes.

The biomes field accepts either a holder set tag or an inline list of ids, so I'll emit it as a list. content.thinking:
I'm drafting a real flight test script for worldgen, modeled on the datapack-real version. It needs to verify a showcase world generates structures correctly, keep the directory around to inspect logs after shutdown, and confirm region files actually get written to the dimension folder to prove chunks were saved.

For the "broken" flight, I'm planning deliberately malformed worldgen files across 1.21.11 and 26.2: a biome using legacy int colors with an unsupported effects key, a configured_feature missing required fields, a structure_set with invalid spacing/separation values, and a dimension referencing a nonexistent biome -- each designed to trigger fatal registry errors at server startup.

I expect the server to either crash with a datapack load failure or refuse to proceed without safe mode, so I'll record whatever boot failure or error logs result, along with the validator's per-file error output, doing one flight per version with all four broken files together rather than isolating each one.

For performance testing, I'm planning forceload checks across 5x5 chunk areas in both crystal/noise and flatland worlds, plus a vanilla nether baseline since nether is enabled by default, polling with `execute in` loaded-checks at far corners to determine when generation completes -- possibly chaining multiple corner and center checks together so a single poll only passes once everything has loaded.

I expect a reply confirming the forceload region, then plan polling steps and probes within crystal — summoning a marker to check its surface position, and using a locate biome command to confirm the nearest crystal_plains biome.

Next I plan locate biome checks for amethyst_hills and a structure ruin locate, then a template placement at (0,200,0), expecting no error messages while verifying the ruin's chest exists at (3,201,3) with the correct loot table. Finally I move on to testing structure placement.

I'm sketching out further test commands: placing the ruin structure at (8,64,8) checking for failure messages, optionally placing an amethyst_ore feature at (8,0,8), optionally checking the crystal_plains biome at origin, and setting up a forceload region for the flatland dimension.

I continue with checks like confirming a grass_block at (8,6,8) in the flatland dimension, a nether baseline forceload (optional since nether may be disabled), and verifying the go_crystal function exists. For natural structure generation, I reason that with the given spacing and separation settings, a ruin should likely generate within the forceloaded area, but since I can't directly assert its presence, using `locate structure` is a reasonable proxy to confirm registration and placement work correctly in the biome.

For timing, each area takes up to 10 seconds of polling across 40 polls at 250ms intervals, so three areas plus commands adds up to roughly 60-80 seconds total, well within the default 420-second timeout. I'm also keeping default memory settings (around 1024 xmx, 1800 rss cap) unless something specific requires adjustment. After the flight completes, I plan to scan the full log for error patterns to catch anything that went wrong post-completion.

Since the tooling supports it, I'll fly all six versions for the showcase, each taking about 1-1.5 minutes, while expecting 1.21.11 and 26.2 (and possibly 1.21.1) to be broken. Time to write the script.

I need to cover versions and the feature matrix with unknown-value failures and blockState handling, then NBT round-trip tests across all tag types including modified UTF-8 edge cases, gzip decoding, determinism, and malformed-input rejection. I also want a real vanilla structure read test — reading the actual igloo/top.nbt from the jar on node-2 with my reader, comparing its decoded structure, and re-encoding/reading it back to confirm a true round-trip on real data. Then for the template compiler I need to test shape validation (layer counts, row lengths, unknown characters, void handling, unused palette warnings, loot placement, capacity limits) plus compile-then-read-back checks on size, palette order, and block positions.

For the spec validation layer, I want to confirm the showcase passes on all six versions, that disabling worldgen correctly falls back, and that non-worldgen showcases remain unchanged against golden hashes, including rerunning the existing test file. Finally I'm building an adversarial corpus of showcase mutations, each expected to trigger a specific error: foreign-namespace biomes, unknown features or blocks, denied blocks like command blocks, bad block states, spacing violations, template size/row mismatches, oversized palettes, invalid noise ranges, feature cycles, non-spawnable entities, attempt limits, too many biomes, missing loot or structure references, and possibly a cost-refusal case from stacking expensive settings together.

I'm now working through how cost limits interact with attempt caps to figure out if a refusal case is actually reachable, then sketching more edge cases like unknown particles, misaligned dimension heights, duplicate noise warnings, and version mismatches. I'm also mapping out per-version emitter differences across biome effects, carvers, music formats, foliage settings, dimension type keys, dragon fight flags, patch placement modifiers, tree providers, and lake predicates, all of which need their own golden hash fixtures stored per version.

For validation, I need the file validator to correctly accept well-formed outputs while rejecting named broken files per version, and to confirm that vanilla-style raw files pass or fail depending on target version compatibility. I also want to verify TS/JS equivalence by extending an existing test that compares generated build artifacts to the TypeScript implementation, now including worldgen inputs from the showcase and corpus, and I'm outlining router test cases covering the flag off/on states, honest limit messaging, and versions without worldgen support.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

input.content:
## Cyrus worldgen (R4)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r8` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN 2b, 4.11, R4 "Biomes, structures, dimensions"; research `A2-datapacks.md` (worldgen), `A-content.md`. **Nothing is deployed or switched on.** New flag `CYRUS_WORLDGEN=1`, which only works together with `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO=1` (fail closed; `worldgenOn()` in `lib/cyrus/datapack/route.ts`). Off, every build request, prompt, report and emitted pack is byte-identical to R2 (tests prove it: the R2 golden hashes, the prompt with `datapack` only, the request service object, the check list of non-worldgen packs). Not plan-gated. Host seam: no new Nxeon imports, no new tables, no foreign keys; worldgen packs are ordinary `CyrusProjectAsset` rows (`kind datapack`) whose provenance also carries `worldgen: true` and the summary.

**Scope (decided).** Vanilla data packs cannot safely edit the existing overworld biome mix, so Cyrus world generation lives in the mod's OWN namespace: (1) a custom **dimension** (`dimension_type` + `dimension`, noise generator from a vanilla terrain preset or a superflat generator) whose biome source (`fixed` / `checkerboard` / `multi_noise`) uses only the pack's own biomes; (2) custom **biomes** (climate, colours, music / ambience / particles, natural spawns, features, vanilla carvers); (3) **features** in those biomes (configured + placed: ores, oak-shaped trees, plant patches, lakes, single blocks; vanilla placed features may be listed too); (4) **structures**: block-layout templates compiled deterministically into `.nbt`, placed as single-piece jigsaw structures with `random_spread` structure sets, only in the pack's own biomes.

**Honest limits (shown on the route, in the prompt, in the delivery plan).** World generation loads only when the server starts (Nxeon restarts once after install; `/reload` is not enough); it only shapes NEW chunks; the dimension is reached by the plugin's teleport command or `/execute in <ns>:<dim> run tp ...` (no portal), and it does not exist until that restart.

**Not supported (documented, refused or warned):** editing the overworld / nether / end biomes or terrain; adding features or structures to vanilla biomes (biome modifiers are NeoForge/Fabric-only); merging worldgen from several packs (conflict engine: `datapack.worldgen_collision` / `datapack.worldgen_override`); custom noise settings, density functions, surface rules, carvers, multi-piece jigsaw; custom portals.

### 1. Files (`lib/cyrus/datapack/worldgen/`)
| File | What |
|---|---|
| `spec.ts` | the eight new resource kinds (Zod; part of DataPackSpec v1's resource union, so every v1 spec stays valid and emits the same bytes), `WORLDGEN_LIMITS`, `WORLDGEN_LIMITS_TEXT`, `NOT_SUPPORTED` |
| `versions.ts` | `worldgenFeatures(version)` (the verified differences below), block state tables, DataVersion, vanilla noise ranges (from `data/worldgen-data.json`) |
| `emit.ts` | per-version emitters (biome, dimension_type, dimension, configured / placed features, jigsaw structure + generated template pool, structure set, template `.nbt`) |
| `nbt.ts` | deterministic NBT writer (Java modified UTF-8, fixed key order) + STORED gzip (mtime 0: the bytes never depend on the zlib build) + an independent reference reader (bounded: 8 MB, depth 32) |
| `template.ts` | structure template compiler: palette chars + y layers of z rows of x chars -> `{DataVersion, size, palette, blocks, entities}`; blocks y/z/x, block entities last (vanilla order); `.` = structure void; chests / trapped chests / barrels can carry an own loot table |
| `check.ts` | semantic checks + engine limits + cost estimate (`checkWorldgen`, called by `validateDataPackSpec` when `ctx.worldgen`), `featureCycle`, denied blocks, spawnable mobs |
| `files.ts` | static file validator for worldgen files (mcdoc fields, value shapes, registry types, cross-file references, structure `.nbt`), used by `validatePackFiles(files, v, { worldgen: true })` |
Data: `lib/cyrus/datapack/data/vanilla-ids.json` gained the worldgen registries (feature / placement / structure / pool element / placement / biome source / generator / trunk + foliage placer / state provider types, block predicate, rule test, sound events, particles, environment attributes) and the vanilla worldgen entries (biomes, configured / placed features, carvers, structures, structure sets, noise settings, template pools, processor lists, dimension types, timelines, world clocks, biome / timeline tags); `mcdoc-subset.json` gained the worldgen dispatches and structs (and camelCase fields, so `SpawnerData.minCount` is known); new `worldgen-data.json` (26 KB: DataVersion per jar, noise preset ranges, block state property tables grouped by signature). All re-derived on node-2 by `scripts/cyrus/datapack-derive.py ids|mcdoc|worldgen` (new mode `worldgen`); the R2 tables are byte-identical except `OldEntityPredicate.catType` (until 1.19, irrelevant).

### 2. Spec (version-neutral; `id` = path in the reserved namespace, references = full ids)
- `dimension_type`: `preset` overworld | nether | end + `minY` (-64..0, x16), `height` (64..384, x16, top <= 320), `logicalHeight`, `ambientLight`, `fixedTime`, `hasSkylight`, `hasCeiling`, `bedWorks`, `respawnAnchorWorks`, `hasRaids`, `coordinateScale` (0.125..8), `monsterSpawnLightLevel`, `monsterSpawnBlockLightLimit`.
- `dimension`: `dimensionType` (own or vanilla) + generator `noise` (`terrain`: overworld, large_biomes, amplified, caves, floating_islands, nether, end; `biomes`: fixed / checkerboard (1-8, scale 0-8) / multi_noise (1-16 points, six climate values each a number or [min, max])) or `flat` (1-16 layers of 1-64, one biome, features on/off; the pack's structure sets become `structure_overrides`).
- `biome`: temperature, downfall, precipitation, frozen, colours (sky, fog, water, water fog, grass, foliage, dry foliage, grass modifier), music, ambient loop, mood, additions, particle (11 option-less particles), spawns (max 16, an allowlist of natural mobs), features (max 24: own or vanilla placed features, per decoration step), carvers (max 4 vanilla).
- `configured_feature`: `ore` (1-4 targets: block or #block tag -> block state; size 1-32), `tree` (straight trunk + blob canopy; heights, radius), `patch` (1-8 weighted blocks, tries 1-96, spreads), `lake` (water / lava + barrier), `block`.
- `placed_feature`: `count` (1-64 or range), `rarity`, `in_square`, `biome`, `heightmap`, `height_range` (uniform / trapezoid; absolute / above bottom / below top), `surface_water_depth`, `would_survive` (max 10 modifiers).
- `structure_template`: `size` [x,y,z] each 1..48 (max volume 48x48x48), `palette` (max 32 one-char entries), `layers`; at most 32768 stored blocks and 16 loot containers.
- `structure`: own template, own biomes (1-16), step, terrain adaptation (none / beard_thin / beard_box / bury), heightmap, `yOffset` -32..32.
- `structure_set`: 1-4 own structures with weights, `spacing` 8-64 chunks, `separation` < spacing, `salt`, spread type, frequency.
- Pack caps: 2 dimensions, 2 dimension types, 16 biomes, 32 configured + 32 placed features, 8 templates, 8 structures, 4 structure sets.

### 3. Per-version differences (VERIFIED on the real jars, 2026-10-10)
Method as in R2: the data generator of every pinned jar dumped the vanilla worldgen files; the same files (`plains`, `cherry_grove`, `swamp`, `soul_sand_valley` biomes, `overworld` / `the_nether` / `the_end` dimension types, `oak`, `ore_iron`, `patch_grass`, `flower_default`, `lake_lava`, placed features, `pillager_outpost` structure + set + pool, `noise_settings`) were compared across versions and against vanilla-mcdoc, the registries were diffed, and then the emitted packs were booted (section 6).

| Difference | Versions | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Biome `carvers` is a map `{"air": [...]}` -> a list | 1.21.1 vs 1.21.2+ | vanilla `plains.json`; mcdoc `CarversPerStep` |
| Biome `effects.music` single object -> weighted list `[{data, weight}]`; `music_volume` added | <1.21.4 vs 1.21.4+ | vanilla `cherry_grove.json` (1.21.4 and 1.21.8) |
| `effects.dry_foliage_color` | 1.21.5+ | vanilla `swamp.json` 1.21.8; mcdoc |
| ENVIRONMENT ATTRIBUTES: sky / fog / water fog colours, music, ambient sounds and particles move from biome `effects` to `attributes` (`minecraft:visual/sky_color`, `minecraft:audio/background_music`, `minecraft:audio/ambient_sounds`, `minecraft:visual/ambient_particles`, ...); `effects` keeps water / grass / foliage / dry foliage + modifier; colours become `"#rrggbb"` strings | <1.21.11 vs 1.21.11+ | vanilla biomes 1.21.11 / 26.x; registry `environment_attribute` (48 ids in 1.21.11, +3 in 26.2) |
| dimension_type: `ultrawarm`, `natural`, `piglin_safe`, `bed_works`, `respawn_anchor_works`, `has_raids`, `fixed_time`, `effects` -> attributes (`gameplay/bed_rule`, `gameplay/respawn_anchor_works`, `gameplay/can_start_raid`, ...) + `has_fixed_time`, `skybox`, `cardinal_light`, `timelines`; `cloud_height` 1.21.6-1.21.10 | <1.21.11 vs 1.21.11+ | vanilla dimension types; mcdoc `DimensionType` |
| dimension_type `default_clock` + REQUIRED `has_ender_dragon_fight` (Cyrus always writes false) | 26.1+ | vanilla `the_end.json` 26.1 |
| `random_patch` / `flower` features REMOVED: a patch is a `simple_block` feature placed with `count` + `random_offset` (trapezoid int provider) + a block filter (vanilla `patch_grass` -> `grass`) | <26.1 vs 26.1+ | registry `worldgen/feature`; vanilla `patch_grass_plain` 26.2 (mcdoc is stale here: no `#[until]`) |
| tree `dirt_provider` + `force_dirt` -> `below_trunk_provider` (rule-based, required from 26.2) | <26.1 vs 26.1+ | vanilla `oak.json`; mcdoc `TreeConfig` |
| lake `can_place_feature`, `can_replace_with_air_or_fluid`, `can_replace_with_barrier` (required) | 26.2 | vanilla `lake_lava.json` 26.2; mcdoc |
| structure template DataVersion 3955 / 4189 / 4440 / 4671 / 4790 / 4903 | 1.21.1 / 1.21.4 / 1.21.8 / 1.21.11 / 26.1.2 / 26.2 | `version.json` `world_version` of each jar |
| Unchanged 1.21.1 .. 26.2 (emitted identically): ore config, placed feature modifiers used, jigsaw structure, structure set (`random_spread`), template pool, noise preset ranges (overworld -64/384, nether 0/128, ...), structure file layout | all | vanilla files hash-compared |

### 4. Validation (spec checks + file checks + engine limits)
Spec: a pack with worldgen gets the extra check id `worldgen` (packs without keep their exact R2 report). `references`: own refs resolve to the right kind; biome sources, structures and structure sets use ONLY own biomes / structures (`own_only`); vanilla refs exist in this version (blocks, block tags, placed / configured features, carvers, sound events, particles, entity types, dimension types; `missingIdReason` says "needs X or newer / removed after"). `worldgen`: the dimension type's height range contains the terrain preset's (`noise_range`), top <= 320, flat layers fit, block state properties and values exist (`block_state`, from blocks.json), denied blocks (command / structure / jigsaw blocks, structure void, barrier, spawners incl. trial, vault, portals, end gateway, moving piston, piston head, TNT, fire, test blocks, light), natural-spawn allowlist (`not_spawnable`), template shape, loot containers point at own loot tables, **feature order cycles** (`feature_order_cycle`: two biomes of one dimension listing features in opposite orders; Minecraft refuses to start), separation < spacing; warnings for unused biomes, structures without a set, duplicate climate points, no dimension, missing `in_square` / `biome` modifiers, shared salts. `limits`: the counts above, `count x patch tries` <= 256 per placed feature, <= 1024 attempts per biome per chunk, the template caps, and the **cost estimate**.

Cost estimate (`worldgen.cost`, heuristic per chunk: 1 = superflat, 10 = vanilla overworld terrain): terrain (flat 1, end 5, nether 8, floating islands 8, overworld / large biomes 10, caves 12, amplified 14) + 0.5 x the worst biome's feature load (attempts x weight: ore size/16, tree 1.5, lake 3, patch 0.05 per try, vanilla placed feature flat 4 attempts) + structures (average template blocks / 500 x 64 / spacing^2 x frequency). Classes: low <= 20, medium <= 40, high <= 100 (warn), above 100 refused. Each class carries a per-server recommendation (section 6). There is no custom noise router or density function at all, so an absurd terrain generator cannot be expressed.

Files (`files.ts`, on emitted packs and on demand): mcdoc fields of biome, effects, spawners, dimension type, dimension, generator, biome source, flat settings, configured feature + config of the subset types, placed feature + modifiers, jigsaw structure (Structure + jigsaw tables), structure set + `random_spread`, template pool + element; value shapes (colour type per version, carvers map / list, music single / weighted, min_y / height x16, separation < spacing); registry types (catches `random_patch` on 26.x); vanilla ids; **cross-file references** (a dimension's biomes, placed -> configured features, structure -> template pool -> template `.nbt`, sets -> structures, flat structure overrides must be files of the same pack); structure `.nbt`: readable gzip + NBT, DataVersion not newer than the target, size 1..48, palette names are blocks, every block inside the size with a valid palette index (vanilla `palettes` lists accepted). Imports keep worldgen files `not_checked` unless asked (R2 behaviour).

### 5. Router, build service, portal, delivery
- **Router** (`datapack/route.ts`): flag on, the adapter's existing `worldgen` rule (biomes, dimensions, "world gen", custom / new structures) joins the data pack rules: `decideDataPackRoute` returns `worldgen: true` + the one-line honest limit (`WORLDGEN_LIMIT_MESSAGE`, <= 300 chars), a change of a mod whose packs already have worldgen keeps it (`existingWorldgen`, `hasWorldgenDatapacks`), a version without verified worldgen data gets a notice and the rest of the route; `routeWithDataPack` replaces the adapter's "not built yet" warning with the honest limit. Flag off: exactly R2.
- **Build request** (`assets/request.ts`, `modbuilder/create.ts`): `service.worldgen = true` and `ModBuild.cyrus.assets.datapack.worldgen = true` only when routed (absent otherwise); no plan lookup.
- **Build service** (`services/modbuilder/{textures.js,datapacks.js,prompts.js,server.js,worldgen-example.json,datapack-spec.js}`): `assets.worldgen` (boolean, needs `assets.datapack`, 400 otherwise; switched off with a note on a version without worldgen data); the `WORLD GENERATION` subsection is appended after `DATA PACK` only when both are on (fixed text; replaces the R2 "not possible" line; the limits, every field, the engine limits, how the plugin teleports: `Bukkit.getWorld(new NamespacedKey(ns, dim))`, null until the restart, never `WorldCreator`); `checkWorkspaceDatapacks(..., { worldgen })` (kept specs of a change are checked with worldgen allowed, as they were valid when made); a soft check flags `new WorldCreator(`; `pack.worldgen { dimensions, cost }` in the asset result; prompt version `mb-datapack-2026-10-10.1+mb-worldgen-2026-10-10.1`. The generated `datapack-spec.js` (now 820 KB) was regenerated on node-2 and is equivalence-tested. The image needs `worldgen-example.json` (Dockerfile updated, image NOT rebuilt).
- **Portal sync** (`assets/sync.ts`, `sync-deps.ts`, `datapack/sync.ts`): re-validation passes `worldgen: worldgenOn(env)` (flag off -> the pack is dropped with a reason); provenance gets `worldgen: true` + the summary (dimensions, biomes, structures, templates, cost); `MbAssets.datapacks[].worldgen`.
- **Delivery** (`datapack/deliver.ts`): worldgen packs are `apply: "restart"` (never `minecraft:reload`; a reload apply is an error), skipped unless `CYRUS_WORLDGEN` is on, and the plan's notes say: restart once, only NEW chunks, reach `<dims>` with the mod's teleport command (no portal, not before the restart), the first start takes a few seconds longer. `rebuildForDelivery` rebuilds with the recorded `worldgen` flag. The NxLabs page has no data pack lines yet (R2 remaining step 3); nothing there promises instant availability.
- **Conflict engine** (`conflicts/engine.ts`): worldgen folders (`worldgen/*`, `dimension`, `dimension_type`, `structure`) never stack: the same own id in two packs = `datapack.worldgen_collision` (blocking), a vanilla worldgen id replaced = `datapack.worldgen_override` (warn for one pack, blocking for two). Tested in the mutation corpus (dimension + biome cases).
- **Test Flight** runner `tf-lite-3`: per-RCON-step wall time in the evidence (`[rss N MB, M ms]`) and `world.generateStructures` (default stays off).
